Subject: Dedicated capacity intake: session velocity and burst taxonomy (AuroraAI)

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks for picking this up. We're evaluating reserved/dedicated capacity with Redwood for the next phase of AuroraAI's conversational product. To help your sizing run, I attached a one-day sample of production telemetry (aurora-telemetry-sample.csv) — it has anonymized session ids, timestamps, prompt length, response length, and whether the request was a chat or embedding.

High-level context:
- Product: multi-turn chat assistant (customer support & knowledge) + an embeddings-based reranker for search.
- Traffic shape: daily morning peak around 09:00–11:00 PT, secondary smaller peak 14:00–15:00 PT, irregular spikes tied to product announcements.
- Current infra: mixed GPU pool, but we'd like predictable committed capacity for Q3 rollout.

We don't have your exact questionnaire yet — can you send the fields you need? Main asks from our side: clear mapping from sample telemetry -> recommended GPU SKUs / commit sizing, and rough cost delta for quantized models vs full fp16.

Can we also schedule a 30–45m sizing workshop next week? Samir (cc'd) will bring the telemetry export.

Thanks,
Sally Wong
Head of Infrastructure
AuroraAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake: session velocity and burst taxonomy (AuroraAI)

Hi Sally —

Appreciate the sample — this is exactly the sort of telemetry that helps. I've attached a short workbook (redwood-dedicated-questionnaire.xlsx) that captures the precise fields we use to size a dedicated pool. If you can fill as many as possible before the workshop, we'll accelerate the draft sizing.

Key fields we need (short form):
1) Traffic windows: which hour-of-day buckets are peak (you mentioned 09:00–11:00 PT) and typical weekend vs weekday multipliers.
2) Concurrency profile: observed sessions concurrently active (P50, P95, P99, and an estimate of true peak instantaneous concurrency). If you have a 1min or 5min time-series, paste it.
3) Prompt/response token distribution: percentiles (P50/P75/P95) for both prompts and responses, and average token count per turn.
4) Session depth: avg turns per session, and percent of sessions reaching >5 turns.
5) Model mix: fraction of requests that call small vs medium vs large model families; embedding batch size and frequency.
6) KV cache behavior: percent of requests that can hit a prefix cache (multi-turn chat benefits heavily).
7) SLA tolerance: P99 latency budget, acceptable tail (e.g., 250ms/500ms/1s), and whether soft degradation (fallback to cheaper model) is acceptable.
8) Data residency / encryption notes and whether you need dedicated KMS/HSM integration.

If some of these are hard to pull, send whatever you have and we'll make conservative assumptions for the sizing workshop. Proposed next steps:
- Please send the completed workbook and any export to the Drive link you prefer.
- I'll draft an initial GPU mapping (SKU-level) based on the sample and assumptions; Marissa will prepare a short deck mapping commit tiers to expected sustained RPS under different hit-rate assumptions.

I've suggested two slots for a 30m workshop: Thu 4/15 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 4/16 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works best?

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—Grace O'Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 22:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake: session velocity and burst taxonomy (AuroraAI)

Grace — thanks, attaching some quick answers inline below and a link to a fuller dump in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E-telemetry

> 1) Traffic windows
Morning peak: 09:00–11:00 PT (roughly 35–40% of daily volume)
Afternoon: 14:00–15:00 PT (10–12%)
Weekends: ~0.5x weekday baseline except during promotional events

> 2) Concurrency profile
P50 concurrent sessions: 48
P95: 120
P99: 420
Estimated instantaneous true peak (1-min agg during last product announce): ~620 concurrent sessions
(we can supply a 5-min series in the Drive folder)

> 3) Prompt/response token distribution
Prompts: median 95 tokens, P75 140, P95 260
Responses: median 320 tokens, P75 480, P95 980
Average tokens per turn: ~415

> 4) Session depth
Avg turns per session: 3.2
% sessions >5 turns: ~8%

> 5) Model mix
Chat medium models: ~70%
Chat large models (long-form answers / policy reasoning): ~20%
Embeddings (reranker/upsert batches): ~10% (embedding batches often aggregated into jobs of 16–64)

> 6) KV cache behavior
Estimated prefix cache hit: ~30–40% (depends on personalization layer)

> 7) SLA tolerance
Target P95 latency: <250ms for short responses (<=200 tokens), allow up to 1s for >500-token responses. For tail, we prefer graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) over hard failures.

> 8) Data residency
All data stays in us-west; we need KMS integration for key rotation.

We'll upload a CSV with 7 days of 1-min aggregated concurrency and a histogram of prompt/response lengths by EOD Friday. If you need any additional fields from our side, call them out.

Thanks — Samir
Staff SRE, AuroraAI

Samir / Sally — this is great, thanks for the early answers and the Drive link. A few quick notes based on your numbers and our sizing heuristics:

- We'll run two candidate maps for the workshop: a conservative commit (assume P99 peak 620, KV hit 30%, no aggressive batching) and an optimistic commit (assume sustained P95 120, KV hit 40%, embedding batching at 32).
- Early SKU hypothesis: 4x A100S or 8x A10G-equivalent for the conservative map (final SKU depends on model family selection + quantization).
- Cost/perf levers we'll test in the workshop: per-session KV caching levels, model fanout (auto-fallback to smaller model at >500ms tail), and embedding batching targets.

I'll schedule the 30m workshop for Fri 4/16 at 09:00 PT (tentative calendar invite sent). Marissa — can you prepare the short deck mapping the two candidate commit tiers to expected sustained RPS and rough monthly $ estimate? Karthik — please sketch a fallback routing plan we can show the customer (model variants + region failover).

Samir — once we receive the 7-day 1-min CSV, we'll plug it into the sizing workbook and circulate a draft GPU-sku mapping before the workshop.

Related: HubSpot deal is here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7832 — I added the workshop note to the timeline.

Thanks all — speak tomorrow.

—Grace
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
